reason: Conversation 1 went straight to the sensible first step (thermostat setting and food against the rear vent), got the two key facts in one question, correctly concluded it was very likely settings/loading rather than a part, advised a mid setting and clear vents, and appropriately reserved engineer referral for persistent freezing without naming parts. Conversation 2 opened with an unnecessary 'switch it off and unplug it' instruction, led with an unsupported and wrong-headed defrost-fault/iced-evaporator theory (which doesn't fit a working freezer and food freezing at the rear inlet), pushed a disruptive full manual defrost of a rammed fridge before checking settings, and never asked about the dial until the customer volunteered it. Conversation 2 also handled the follow-up poorly by again attributing residual freezing to a defrost fault instead of a possible damper/thermostat issue warranting an engineer, and its 'back wall where you're standing' and 'thaw within a few hours' comments were sloppy.
